recipes.name: Butternut Squash Bake
ingredients_raw: 1 (4 pound) butternut squash - peeled, seeded, and cubed
sea salt and ground black pepper to taste

steps.text: Preheat the oven to 425 degrees F (220 degrees C).

Toss squash, blue cheese, ½ cup bread crumbs, onion, olive oil, and thyme together in a bowl; season with sea salt and black pepper. Transfer squash mixture to a large baking dish; sprinkle with remaining ¼ cup bread crumbs.
Bake in the preheated oven until top is lightly browned, 35 to 40 minutes.

raw_recipe.headline: Butternut Squash Bake
raw_recipe.description: This butternut squash bake recipe with blue cheese features Italian bread crumbs, onion, thyme, and olive oil for a tasty, savory vegetarian main dish.

review.reviewBody: This was AMAZING! The only change I made was that I used crushed corn flakes & Italian seasoning instead of seasoned bread crumbs and did not add salt & pepper. This is SO good that my husband and kids immediately asked if I would make this again. Thank you!

This is DELICIOUS and easy! I substituted the blue cheese with feta instead. I covered the dish while it baked in aluminum foil until the last 10 minutes. In the future, I would add pine nuts and maybe a little bit more bread crumbs on top, but it was such a hit as is!

This was a great find. I enjoy a bit more texture and wanted it meat free, so I added a meatless crumble, sauteed with minced onion and bellpepper. 
Grated Parmigiana in addition to the blue cheese.

Made this for my daughter and I with feta cheese. It was very good! I would use a little less oil, a little more feta and I would broil the top before serving. I used dried thyme and shallots instead of the yellow onion. I loved reading everyone’s little tweaks and changes to this recipe. I feel like it’s a no fail dish that will be good to bring to a dinner where you’re responsible for a veg or side dish. Comfort food- yet... :-)

I never ate Butternut Squash before but hubby wanted to try it. This recipe sounded good, and it was. The only cheese I had in the house was grated parmesan, so I used that. We don't like blue cheese anyway. I diced the onion rather than minced. This turned out excellent. I cut it into bite sized pieces so it only took 30 min. I'll definitely make this again.

I've used this recipe for years. It is great as is. My variations have included adding fresh cranberries and apples to it, and/or sweet Italian sausage cooked and out of the casing. I've omitted the bread crumbs and/or cheese depending on dietary needs at the time and it still turns out great.

This is very good. 
I made only 1/2 of the recipe. My squash was only 2 lbs. 
I did change the recipe just a little bit to use what I had on hand. 
I used garlic salt in place of just salt.
I added feta instead of the blue cheese
Italian bread crumbs instead of plain
I baked a little longer and took some of the finished baked butternut and pureed it. I tossed it with penne. Very good.
The rest will be eaten as a side dish.

This recipe came out dry and a little boring. I baked covered for 20 min and uncovered for last 10 min. 

It perked up when I added extra salt and pepper. It also got a boost after I drizzled it with almond milk. 

Subbed 2 lbs of squash for 1 bushel of kale and 1 can of navy beans, which were included to turn this side dish into an entree.

Next time, I will add something for more moisture before baking, either extra olive oil, almond milk, just mayo (vegan mayo), or regular mayo. Will keep the greens and beans for color, variety, and protein - could use black beans instead of navy beans, too.
I also added 1/2 red pepper, 1/2 green pepper, lots of garlic, along with the blue cheese I added feta and Parmesan cheese. Yummy!

Excellent with changes. Reduced oil to 2 Tablespoons, added 1/2 teaspoon garlic powder, skipped the cheese and extra crumbs on top. YUMMMMYY Also a recipe on here called 'simple roasted butternut squash' is great. This is my new favorite though, can't wait to make again. Thank you so much for submitting this :)
This was very good. My squash was cut in quite small pieces and the cooking time was a lot shorter and I thought the oven was too hot. Will bake at no more than 400 and maybe 375 for a lot less time.
By far the best squash recipe I have ever tried. The unusual flavors are just amazing. If I’m out of blue cheese, I used feta and it is just as good.

I made this recipe pretty closely as written, making sure to dice the squash in small bites so they would bake through quickly. Now that i've made it once, I think the comments recommending using stuffing bread cubes sounds fabulous and would like to try that in the near future.
I used italian cheese mixed with plain flour and mustard powder for the sauce instead of blue cheese. And I used red onions instead of yellow. Perfect!

As noted in other reviews, I needed to bake a bit longer. Also used parmesan cheese, as some in my family are averse to blue cheese. Very good, though, and I plan to try it on the clan at Thanksgiving!
Made just as directed. I did have to bake it much longer than the 40min.
I love this recipe! A standard for the Fall and Thanksgiving dinner of course!
this is one of our favorites! I've made it by the recipe many times and have tried a few different substitutions here and there. I will definitely be keeping this recipe for future use!

I have added spicy Italian sausage or chorizo occasionally to delicious effect. My husband loves it. I’ve used goat cheese when out of blue cheese. And, when doing paleo, I swapped almond meal mixed with Italian spices for bread crumbs.
Made mine for the office Friendsgiving Lunch - it was a huge hit!
